mainTopic: What a יבם acquires through העראה, especially whether the יבמה may eat תרומה, plus רבי נתן's view on the wife of a deaf כהן
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier statement: contact below a set minimum is 'only a kiss' and carries no punishment, a view that disagrees with שמואל. It then asks what the משנה means when it says a יבם 'acquires' his יבמה even through העראה. רב says he acquires her for everything. שמואל says he acquires her only for what the יבום section mentions, so the question is whether she may eat תרומה. The גמרא gives two versions of where they argue: about a woman who was only engaged to the brother, or about one who was fully married. In each version a ברייתא about a deaf-mute husband and a deaf-mute יבם is brought against שמואל. In the first version שמואל answers by rereading the ברייתא. In the second version the challenge against him stands as a קשיא. Next comes a ברייתא about a son born to the wife of a כהן who became a חרש, where רבי נתן and חכמים argue about whether she keeps eating after the son dies. רבה's explanation of רבי נתן is rejected by אביי. רב יוסף's explanation also ends with a קשיא. The amud closes by quoting the משנה's line about anyone who has relations with one of the עריות, and רב עמרם begins reporting a teaching of רב ששת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Less than the minimum is only a kiss
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier statement: contact below the set minimum is only a 'kiss,' and there is no punishment for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: From this point and beyond, it is nothing more than a kiss, and he is exempt for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that began just before this section. It says that contact less than the stated minimum does not count as intercourse at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier statement set a minimum amount of contact for העראה. Anything below that line is called 'just a kiss.' A kiss is not a forbidden act of intercourse, so there is no punishment for it.

keyTerms.meaning: from here and beyond: anything past the line just set
a kiss: here, contact too slight to count as intercourse

phrases.english: From this point forward, it is only a kiss,
and he is exempt for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a definition of העראה that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Contact less than the set minimum is only a kiss and is not punishable.

steps.title: This view disagrees with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the statement just given disagrees with שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short comment. The statement it just finished does not fit with what שמואל holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that even very slight, outer contact can make a person liable. The statement just quoted calls that kind of contact 'only a kiss' with no punishment. So the two views clash.
steps.whatToRemember: The minimum for העראה is debated. This view says less than the minimum is just a kiss, while שמואל holds that even outer contact counts.

phrases.english: And it disagrees with Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that step 1 conflicts with שמואל's position.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The statement in step 1 and שמואל hold different views about the minimum for liability.

steps.title: What does 'acquired' mean in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a יבם acquires his יבמה through either the first stage or a full act, and asks what 'acquired' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: both one who does the first stage and one who finishes have acquired her. What does 'acquired' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. It asks how far the word 'acquired' reaches, which sets up the argument that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that even העראה, the first stage, makes the יבם acquire the יבמה. It does not say what that acquiring achieves. Is she now his wife in every way, or only for certain laws?

keyTerms.meaning: one who does העראה, the first stage of intercourse
one who finishes the full act
acquired: made her his wife through יבום

phrases.english: Both one who engages in the first stage and one who completes have acquired.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, about a יבם who lives with his יבמה.

phrases.english: What does 'acquired' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the minimum act and turns to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much of a marriage the יבם gains through העראה.

steps.title: רב: he acquires her for everything
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the יבם acquires her completely. She is his wife in every way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: he acquired her for everything.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer. Even העראה makes the יבמה the יבם's full wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'For everything' covers all the laws of a wife. For example, if the יבם is a כהן, she may eat תרומה like any כהן's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: for everything: in every legal way

phrases.english: Rav said: he acquired for everything,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: העראה makes the יבמה the יבם's wife in every way.

steps.title: שמואל: only for the laws written in the יבום section
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the יבם acquires her only for what the Torah's יבום section mentions: inheriting his brother and freeing her from further יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: he acquired her only for the things said in the section: to inherit his brother's property, and to free her from יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a narrower answer. העראה works only for the specific results the יבום section talks about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל names two results. The יבם inherits his dead brother's estate. And if the יבם then dies leaving children from another wife, she does not need יבום again. Other wifely laws, like eating תרומה, are not automatically included.

keyTerms.meaning: the Torah section, here the section about יבום
levirate marriage of a brother's widow

phrases.english: and Shmuel said: he did not acquire except
for the matters stated in the section:
to inherit his brother's property,
and to exempt her from levirate marriage.
phrases.notes: If he later dies leaving children from another wife, she is free and needs no further יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: לֹא קָנָה אֶלָּא לִדְבָרִים הָאֲמוּרִים בַּפָּרָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an answer that opposes רב's answer in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: העראה works only for inheritance and for freeing her from further יבום.

steps.title: Where they really argue: an engaged woman, not a married one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the argument. If the brother had fully married her, everyone agrees she eats תרומה. They argue only if she was just engaged to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was married to the dead brother, everyone agrees she may eat, since she was already eating from the start. Where they argue is when she was only engaged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down exactly where רב and שמואל argue. It is setting up the reasons each one gives next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a נשואה married to a כהן. She already ate תרומה, so the יבם's העראה just lets her keep doing so. A woman who was only engaged (ארוסה) did not yet eat תרומה. So the question is whether העראה can give her a new right she never had.

keyTerms.meaning: betrothal: the first stage of marriage, before living together
she eats, here meaning she may eat תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the text never says the word, 'eating' here means eating תרומה, which only a כהן's household may do.

phrases.english: From marriage, everyone agrees she partakes,
phrases.notes: She eats תרומה. The dead brother and the יבם are כהנים.

phrases.english: since she was already partaking from the outset.
Where they disagree is from betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the argument of steps 4-5 to one specific case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow who was married eats תרומה after העראה according to all. The argument is only about one who was engaged.

steps.title: רב's reason: the Torah treats every יבום act as a full one
steps.stepSummary: רב says the engaged יבמה may eat תרומה, because the Torah counts even an accidental act of יבום like an intentional one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: she eats, since the Torah included even an unintentional act as if it were intentional.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains why he lets the engaged woman eat תרומה. The Torah gives every kind of יבום act full strength.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists acts that still count as יבום, such as an unintentional act. To רב, this shows the Torah gives any act of יבום the full power of a real marriage. So העראה makes her a full wife, and a כהן's full wife eats תרומה.

phrases.english: Rav said: she may partake,
since the Merciful One included
unwitting intercourse like intentional.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: אוֹכֶלֶת, דְּהָא רַבִּי רַחֲמָנָא בִּיאַת שׁוֹגֵג כְּמֵזִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's ruling and reason for the case named in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An engaged יבמה eats תרומה after העראה, because the Torah treats every act of יבום as a full one.

steps.title: שמואל's reason: the יבם replaces the husband but doesn't go beyond him
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the Torah's widening only puts the יבם in the husband's place. It cannot give him more than the husband had.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: when the Torah included these acts, it was to set him in the husband's place. To make him stronger than the husband, no.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers רב's reasoning. The engaged woman may not eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל agrees that the Torah counts these acts as יבום. But their job is only to let the יבם step into his brother's shoes. The dead brother was only engaged to her, so she did not eat תרומה with him. The יבם cannot give her more than his brother could.

keyTerms.meaning: to set him up, to establish him

steps.whatToRemember: רב says העראה makes the יבמה a full wife, so even one who was engaged eats תרומה. שמואל says the יבם only replaces the husband, so she eats only if she already ate with the brother.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that the יבם 'stands in the husband's place but not beyond' is a key way to think about what יבום really is: a continuation of the brother's marriage, not a fresh, stronger one.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: when the Merciful One included,
it was to establish him in place of the husband,
to strengthen him beyond the husband, no.
phrases.notes: The engaged woman never ate תרומה with the dead brother, so the יבם can't let her start.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: כִּי רַבִּי רַחֲמָנָא, לְאוֹקְמֵיהּ בִּמְקוֹם בַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's reasoning in step 7 by limiting what the Torah's widening does.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An engaged יבמה does not eat תרומה after העראה, because the יבם can only replace the husband, not go beyond him.

steps.title: שמואל is consistent with his general rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that שמואל's view here matches a rule he stated elsewhere: whatever the husband could do for her eating תרומה, the יבם can do, and no more.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל is following his own reasoning. רב נחמן said in שמואל's name: wherever the husband lets her eat תרומה, the יבם lets her eat. Wherever the husband does not, the יבם does not either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל's position from the last step is not a one-time idea. It matches a general rule he said elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 שמואל said the יבם only stands in the husband's place. Here that becomes a clear two-sided rule: the יבם's power to let her eat תרומה is exactly the same as the husband's, no more and no less. This sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (this matches what he said elsewhere)
Lets her eat (here: gives her the right to eat תרומה)
The husband, meaning the brother who died

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the exact claim the ברייתא in the next step seems to break.

phrases.english: And שמואל follows his own reasoning,
as רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל:
Any case where the husband lets her eat
phrases.notes: Eat what? תרומה. The גמרא leaves the word out because that's the whole topic.

phrases.english: the יבם lets her eat,
and any case where the husband does not let her eat
the יבם does not let her eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that שמואל's reasoning in step 8 matches a broader rule he holds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יבם's power to let her eat תרומה is exactly the same as the husband's: if the husband could, the יבם can; if not, the יבם cannot.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a deaf-mute husband and a deaf-mute יבם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. A woman engaged to a כהן who became a חרש before the wedding cannot eat תרומה. After he dies, a deaf-mute יבם does let her eat. The ברייתא says the יבם is stronger than the husband here.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: A competent Jewish woman was engaged to a competent כהן. Before he could marry her, he became a deaf-mute. She cannot eat תרומה. If he died and she came before a deaf-mute יבם, she can eat. Here the יבם's power is greater than the husband's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the יבם can do more than the husband, which goes against שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband was only engaged to her, and after he became a חרש his marriage to her could not let her eat. Yet the deaf-mute יבם, whose act happens without real intent (like the accidental יבום in step 7), does let her eat. The ברייתא even says outright that the יבם is stronger than the husband.

keyTerms.meaning: Became a deaf-mute (a חֵרֵשׁ, treated as not mentally competent in הלכה)
He did not manage to marry her (bring her into the full marriage)

steps.confusionAlert: The husband was competent when he got engaged, so the engagement counts. The problem is only that he became a חרש before the wedding, so a wedding by him now cannot let her eat תרומה.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A competent daughter of a ישראל
who was engaged to a competent כהן,
and he did not manage to marry her
before he became a deaf-mute
she does not eat.
If he died, and she came before a deaf-mute יבם
she eats,
and in this the power of the יבם is greater
than the power of the husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that seems to break שמואל's rule from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that the יבם cannot let her eat where the husband could not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא the husband could not let her eat, yet the deaf-mute יבם can. The ברייתא says openly that the יבם is stronger than the husband.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits רב but is hard for שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem: the ברייתא works well for רב but is difficult for שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, for רב this works out. But for שמואל it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge by saying which side the ברייתא helps and which side it hurts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that even יבום without intent counts fully, so the deaf-mute יבם can let her eat even though the husband could not. שמואל said the יבם never gets more than the husband had, but the ברייתא gives him more.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (for one side)
It is difficult (a problem for this view)

phrases.english: Granted, according to רב it works out
but according to שמואל it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב נִיחָא אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוּאֵל קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States outright the problem the ברייתא causes for שמואל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets a deaf-mute יבם give her a right to eat that the husband could not give, which matches רב and goes against שמואל.

steps.title: שמואל rereads the ברייתא: the husband married her first
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers by reading the ברייתא differently. Not marrying before becoming a חרש means she cannot eat. But if he married her and only then became a חרש, she eats, and after his death the deaf-mute יבם also lets her eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל can tell you: say it this way. If he did not manage to marry her before he became a deaf-mute, she cannot eat תרומה. If he married her and afterward became a deaf-mute, she eats. If he died and she came before a deaf-mute יבם, she eats.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge by changing how the ברייתא reads, so the deaf-mute יבם case is about a woman whose husband had fully married her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל's version, the deaf-mute יבם case comes after a husband who married her while he was still competent, so she was already allowed to eat. The יבם only keeps the right the husband gave her. That fits שמואל's rule that the יבם gets no more than the husband had.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (this is how he would answer)
Say it this way (read the source like this)
He married her (fully, not just engaged)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל keeps his rule by reading the ברייתא as a case where the husband fully married her before becoming a חרש. So the deaf-mute יבם only passes on a right she already had. For רב, the ברייתא works as written.

phrases.english: שמואל can say to you:
Say it this way:
If he did not manage to marry her before he became a deaf-mute
she does not eat תרומה,
if he married her and afterward became a deaf-mute
she eats.
If he died and she came before a deaf-mute יבם
she eats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 10-11 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא by adding a missing case (אימא הכי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's deaf-mute יבם case follows a husband who was only engaged, so the יבם gives more than the husband could.
steps.terutzMaskana: The deaf-mute יבם case follows a husband who married her before becoming a חרש. She already could eat, and the יבם only continues that right.

steps.title: What 'in this' means: the deaf-mute יבם is stronger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes שמואל's reading of the ברייתא. The word 'in this' (בזו) means the יבם is stronger than the husband only in one way: a husband who was a חרש from the start cannot feed her תרומה, but a יבם who was a חרש from the start can.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'in this' mean? A husband who was a deaf-mute from the start (before the wedding) cannot let her eat. But a יבם who was a deaf-mute from the start does let her eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing שמואל's answer. It explains exactly which way the ברייתא means when it says the יבם is 'stronger' than the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12, שמואל said the ברייתא speaks about a husband who married her first and only later became a חרש. That leaves the word 'בזו' needing an explanation. The answer: a husband who was a חרש before the wedding never had a marriage that counts for תרומה. A יבם who was always a חרש still lets her eat, because his brother's full marriage is the starting point. So the יבם is not getting more than the husband had. He is standing in the place of a husband who really was married to her.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, from the beginning
A deaf-mute, who in הלכה cannot make a full marriage himself

phrases.english: And what does "in this" mean?
phrases.notes: This refers back to the ברייתא's words: 'in this, the יבם is stronger than the husband.'

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ בַּעַל חֵרֵשׁ מֵעִיקָּרָא — לֹא אוֹכֶלֶת.
phrases.english: That whereas if the husband was a deaf-mute from the start, she does not eat;
whereas if the יבם was a deaf-mute from the start, she eats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading of the ברייתא that שמואל started in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'בזו' seemed to say the יבם gets more power than the husband ever had, which goes against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בזו' only compares a husband who was a חרש from the start with a יבם who was a חרש from the start. The יבם still stands only in place of a husband who was fully married.

steps.title: Second version: engaged woman, everyone agrees she does not eat
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the argument between רב and שמואל: if she was only engaged (אירוסין) to the brother who died, everyone agrees she does not eat תרומה, since she did not eat in her husband's lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: if she comes from engagement only, everyone agrees she does not eat, because she did not eat while her husband was alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a different version of the whole רב and שמואל argument. Here it first sets out the case where both agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the engaged woman is not argued about at all. She never ate תרומה through the husband, so the יבם's ביאה cannot give her something she never had. This sets up the next step, where the real argument is moved to the fully married woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Engagement, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: And some say: if she is a יבמה from engagement,
everyone agrees she does not eat,
since she did not eat in the husband's lifetime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of the argument between רב and שמואל instead of the one already discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From אירוסין, all agree the יבמה does not eat תרומה, because she never ate through her husband.

steps.title: The real argument: a fully married woman and ביאת שוגג
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רב and שמואל argue about a woman who was fully married (נשואין). רב says she eats, since she already ate before. שמואל says she does not, because the Torah counts ביאת שוגג like a deliberate one only for the laws written in the section about יבום, not for everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about a woman from full marriage. רב says: she eats, since she already ate from the start. שמואל says: she does not eat. When the Torah included unwitting ביאה as if it were deliberate, that was only for the matters stated in that section, but not for all matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now lays out the real argument in the second version. Both opinions are given with their reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב looks at her history: she was already eating תרומה as a married woman, so the יבם simply continues that. שמואל limits the Torah's widening: a ביאת שוגג works to complete יבום itself (the laws in that section), but it does not reach other areas like letting her eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Full marriage, the final stage after engagement
The Torah section, here the section about יבום

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not say a ביאת שוגג fails to complete יבום. It does count for יבום. He only says it does not also let her eat תרומה.

phrases.english: Where they argue is a woman from full marriage.
רב says: she eats,
since she was already eating from the start,
and שמואל says: she does not eat,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי רַבִּי רַחֲמָנָא בִּיאַת שׁוֹגֵג כְּמֵזִיד —
phrases.english: because when the Torah included unwitting ביאה as if deliberate,
it was for the matters stated in the section,
but for all other matters, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the agreed case in step 14, this gives the case where they do argue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From נשואין, רב says she eats תרומה. שמואל says a ביאת שוגג by the יבם works only for the laws of יבום, not for תרומה.

steps.title: Challenge from שמואל's own rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: רב נחמן quoted him saying that whatever the husband feeds, the יבם feeds. This woman ate תרומה through her husband, so the יבם should let her eat too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב נחמן say in the name of שמואל: whenever the husband lets her eat, the יבם lets her eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's view in the second version, using a rule שמואל himself said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here she was fully married and did eat through her husband. Read simply, שמואל's rule says the יבם then lets her eat too. That goes against what שמואל just said in step 15, that she does not eat.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (he) say? A way of bringing a challenge

phrases.english: But didn't רב נחמן say in the name of שמואל:
phrases.notes: This is the same rule of שמואל mentioned back in step 9.

phrases.english: Whenever the husband lets her eat, the יבם lets her eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling in step 15 from his own rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a fully married יבמה does not eat תרומה after a ביאת שוגג by the יבם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her husband did let her eat. By שמואל's own rule the יבם should also let her eat, so שמואל contradicts himself.

steps.title: Reread the rule: it is about the type of ביאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads שמואל's rule: any type of ביאה through which a husband could let her eat, the יבם can also use to let her eat. Any type through which a husband could not let her eat, the יבם cannot either. A ביאת שוגג is not a way a husband could marry her, so the יבם's ביאת שוגג does not feed her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it this way: any ביאה through which the husband lets her eat, the יבם lets her eat through it. And any ביאה through which the husband does not let her eat, the יבם does not let her eat through it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing how שמואל's rule should be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not about whether this woman ate before. It is about the kind of act. A husband cannot make a marriage through an unwitting act. So an unwitting act by the יבם, though it completes יבום, does not give her תרומה. That keeps שמואל's view in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Marital relations, here as an act that makes a marriage

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, both agree an engaged woman does not eat. For a fully married woman, רב says she eats. שמואל says the יבם's ביאת שוגג does not feed her, because his rule 'what the husband can do, the יבם can do' is about the type of act, and a husband cannot marry through an unwitting act.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows שמואל's steady approach: the יבם only steps into the husband's place, measured by what a husband's act could do, never beyond it.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: כׇּל בִּיאָה שֶׁהַבַּעַל מַאֲכִיל בָּהּ —
phrases.english: Say: any ביאה through which the husband lets her eat,
the יבם lets her eat through it,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל בִּיאָה שֶׁאֵין הַבַּעַל מַאֲכִיל בָּהּ —
phrases.english: and any ביאה through which the husband does not let her eat,
the יבם does not let her eat through it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: כׇּל בִּיאָה שֶׁהַבַּעַל מַאֲכִיל בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by rereading שמואל's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's rule seemed to mean: if this woman ate through her husband, she eats through the יבם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is about the type of ביאה. Since a husband cannot let her eat through an unwitting act, the יבם's unwitting act does not let her eat either.

steps.title: A ברייתא where a deaf יבם does more than a deaf husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a deaf husband cannot feed his engaged wife תרומה, but a deaf יבם can. This works for רב but is hard for שמואל's second version.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: A competent Jewish woman was engaged to a competent כהן. Before he could marry her, he became a חרש. She does not eat תרומה. If he died and she fell to a deaf יבם, she does eat. So in this way the יבם is stronger than the husband. For רב this is fine, because he can answer the way שמואל answered in the first version. But for שמואל it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's second-version rule, 'whatever a husband can't do, a יבם can't do', with a ברייתא where the יבם does more than the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רב also agrees that an engaged woman does not eat, so he too must reread the ברייתא. He uses the answer from steps 12-13: the husband married her first and only then became a חרש, and 'בזו' compares a husband and a יבם who were each a חרש from the start. שמואל cannot use that answer. Even for a fully married woman, the ברייתא lets a deaf יבם's act, done without real intent, feed her תרומה, but שמואל said in steps 15-17 that such an act counts only for the laws of יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Mentally competent (able to hear and speak)
He became a חרש (deaf-mute, treated as not legally competent)
Granted, this works for one side (a problem for the other side is coming)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first version, it was שמואל who reread the ברייתא (steps 12-13). Now רב borrows that same answer, and שמואל (in the second version) is the one stuck.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A competent daughter of an Israelite
who was engaged to a competent priest,
and he did not manage to marry her before he became a deaf-mute
— she does not eat (teruma).
If he died, and she fell before a deaf-mute yavam
— she eats.

phrases.aramaic: וּבָזוֹ יָפֶה כֹּחַ יָבָם מִכֹּחַ בַּעַל.
phrases.english: And in this, the power of the yavam is greater than the power of the husband.
Granted, according to Rav,
he answers the way it was answered at first.
phrases.notes: This points back to steps 12-13, where שמואל reread the ברייתא (the husband married her first) and explained 'בזו' in the first version.

phrases.english: But according to Shmuel, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's rereading from step 17 with a ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even when the ברייתא is reread as a case of a fully married woman, a deaf יבם's act, done without real intent, lets her eat תרומה. In this version שמואל says an act like that works only for the laws of יבום, not for תרומה.

steps.title: The challenge against שמואל stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: the question on שמואל has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is indeed difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer for שמואל, so the challenge stays unresolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bare 'קשיא' means the question is strong but does not fully knock out the opinion. The second version of שמואל's view is left with an open problem, while רב's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a difficulty (left without an answer)

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, the ברייתא about the deaf יבם is an unanswered problem for שמואל, but not for רב.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 18
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's second version remains difficult because of the ברייתא.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a son born to the wife of a deaf כהן
steps.stepSummary: A woman engaged to a כהן who became a חרש does not eat תרומה. If she has a son from him, she eats. If the son dies, רבי נתן says she still eats and חכמים say she does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A competent Jewish woman was engaged to a competent כהן, and before he married her he became a חרש. She does not eat תרומה. If a son was born to her, she eats. If the son died, רבי נתן says she eats, and חכמים say she does not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about the same deaf-כהן case, adding a son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the son is alive, she eats because of him, since the son of a כהן lets his mother eat. The argument is only about after the son dies: does her right to eat continue?

keyTerms.meaning: A son was born to her

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A competent daughter of an Israelite
who was engaged to a competent priest,
and he did not manage to marry her before he became a deaf-mute
— she does not eat.
If a son was born to her — she eats.
If the son died,
Rabbi Natan says: she eats,
and the Rabbis say: she does not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about a related deaf-כהן case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the son dies: רבי נתן says she eats, and חכמים say she does not.

steps.title: Why does רבי נתן let her keep eating?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי נתן's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי נתן's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי נתן lets her keep eating once her son is gone. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the son dies, the reason she was eating seems to be gone, so רבי נתן's ruling needs an explanation.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Natan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the opinion in step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי נתן lets her eat after the son dies

steps.title: רבה: She already ate
steps.stepSummary: רבה says that since she already ate תרומה in a permitted way, she may keep eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Since she has already eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that her earlier permission to eat carries forward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's idea is that once a woman was allowed to eat תרומה, that right stays with her even after the reason for it is gone.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Since she already ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She keeps eating because she already ate before.

steps.title: אביי: Then a widow of a כהן should also keep eating
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that by רבה's logic, a Jewish woman whose כהן husband died should keep eating. Everyone agrees she doesn't, because his holiness leaves her when he dies. The same should be true when the son dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, a Jewish woman married to a כהן who died should keep eating, since she already ate! Rather, once he died, his holiness left her. Here too, once the son died, his holiness left her!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבה's answer by showing it leads to a result everyone knows is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow of a כהן with no children goes back to being a regular Jewish woman, even though she ate before. So 'she already ate' cannot be a reason. Her right to eat comes from the כהן's holiness, which ends when he (or the son) dies.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (your logic leads to a strange result)
The כהן's holiness that lets her eat

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if so,

phrases.aramaic: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּיסֵּת לְכֹהֵן וּמִית לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: a daughter of an Israelite who married a priest and he died,
let her eat, since she already ate!
Rather, since he died,
his holiness left her.
Here too:
since he (the son) died,
his holiness left her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's answer from step 22
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If eating before were enough, a widow of a כהן would keep eating, and she does not.

steps.title: רב יוסף: רבי נתן holds that marriage to a חרש lets her eat
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a new reason: רבי נתן holds that the נשואין of a חרש let his wife eat תרומה, and he does not make a decree because of the קידושין of a חרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: רבי נתן holds that the marriage (נשואין) of a חרש lets her eat תרומה, and we do not make a decree against the marriage of a חרש because of the engagement (קידושין) of a חרש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף replaces רבה's answer with a new explanation. רבי נתן's reason has nothing to do with the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קידושין were done while the husband was competent, and the נשואין happened after he became a חרש. רבי נתן holds that this נשואין works to let her eat. He does not worry that people will confuse it with the weaker קידושין of a חרש, so she eats on her own right even after the son dies.

keyTerms.meaning: The full marriage done by a חרש
The engagement done by a חרש

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Rabbi Natan holds
that the marriage of a deaf-mute lets her eat teruma,
and we do not decree against the marriage of a deaf-mute
because of the engagement of a deaf-mute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to step 21 after רבה's answer was rejected
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי נתן holds the נשואין of a חרש feed her, with no decree against it.

steps.title: אביי: Then why mention the son?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: if the marriage itself lets her eat, why does the ברייתא mention a son being born?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, why do I need 'a son was born to her'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף: under his reading, the son seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the נשואין alone feed her according to רבי נתן, she should eat even without any son. So why does the ברייתא build the case around a son?

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
If so,
why do I need 'a son was born to her'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's explanation from step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's explanation of רבי נתן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the נשואין alone feed her, the detail about the son is not needed.

steps.title: The son is mentioned because of the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The son is mentioned because of the רבנן's view: for them, she eats only because of the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: the son is in the ברייתא to set up the argument, since for the רבנן the son is her only way to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that the נשואין of a חרש do not feed her, so she eats only while the son lives. The ברייתא builds the case with a son to show where the two sides split: after the son dies, the רבנן say she stops, and רבי נתן says she still eats.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of the view of the Sages

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's reason ('she already ate') was rejected. רב יוסף says רבי נתן lets her eat because the נשואין of a חרש feed תרומה. The son is mentioned only because of the רבנן's view.

phrases.english: Because of the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: The detail is explained as needed for the other opinion in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son detail seemed pointless if the marriage alone feeds her
steps.terutzMaskana: The son is mentioned for the רבנן, who let her eat only because of the son

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי נתן disagree in the first clause?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks why רבי נתן does not argue with the רבנן already at the start of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let רבי נתן disagree with them in the first clause!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף again. If רבי נתן holds that the marriage itself lets her eat, he should argue with the רבנן right at the start of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יוסף, רבי נתן says the נשואין of a חרש are enough to let his wife eat תרומה, even with no son. But the first clause of the ברייתא says that, with no son, she does not eat. That is the רבנן's view. So רבי נתן should already disagree there, but the ברייתא does not show him doing so.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a teaching

phrases.english: And let Rabbi Natan disagree with them
phrases.notes: "Them" means the רבנן, the other side of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: in the first clause!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in Step 26 and points to a new problem with how the ברייתא is arranged.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's explanation that רבי נתן lets the wife eat because of the נשואין alone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי נתן disagrees with the basic reason for her eating, his disagreement should show up already in the first clause, where the רבנן state their view.

steps.title: רבי נתן waited for the רבנן to finish
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that רבי נתן let the רבנן finish their whole statement and only then disagreed with all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He left the רבנן alone until they finished their words, and then he disagreed with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains that רבי נתן did not interrupt. He let the רבנן finish everything and then argued with their whole position at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is about how the ברייתא is arranged, not about the law itself. רבי נתן's disagreement really covers the first clause too. He just states it once, after the רבנן have said everything.

phrases.english: He left the Rabbis alone
until they finished their statement
and then he disagreed with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁבֵיק לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן עַד דִּמְסַיְּימִי מִילְּתַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains how the ברייתא is arranged: רבי נתן's disagreement is placed after the רבנן's full statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי נתן doesn't speak in the first clause, it looks like he agrees with it.
steps.terutzMaskana: He disagrees with all of it but waits until the רבנן finish before speaking.

steps.title: Then רבי נתן should come after 'if the son died'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if רבי נתן waited until the end, the ברייתא should first say 'if the son died, she does not eat' and only then quote רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it teach: 'If the son died, she does not eat.' Then: 'רבי נתן says: she eats!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's answer. If רבי נתן really waited for the רבנן to finish, his words should come after the רבנן's last ruling, the case where the son died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא as we have it, רבי נתן speaks before the רבנן have stated their ruling about the son dying. That doesn't match the idea that he waited for them to finish. The order of the ברייתא does not fit רב יוסף's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach, it should have said

phrases.english: If so, let it teach:
'If the son died, she does not eat,'
phrases.notes: This is the wording the גמרא thinks the ברייתא should have had, so that the רבנן finish first.

phrases.english: 'Rabbi Natan says: she eats!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that רבי נתן waited for the רבנן to finish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he waited, his view would be placed after the רבנן's last ruling, but the ברייתא places it earlier.

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that this question on רב יוסף has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this back-and-forth by saying the question stands. No answer is given for רב יוסף's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying קשיא means the challenge is real and unresolved. The order of the ברייתא remains a problem for רב יוסף's reading of רבי נתן. Still, a קשיא is weaker than a full rejection.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the question stays unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף explained רבי נתן as holding that the marriage of a חרש itself lets his wife eat תרומה. But the order of the ברייתא does not fit this well, and the גמרא leaves it as a קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: A קשיא is not the same as תיובתא. קשיא means the question has no answer yet. It does not mean the view has been completely knocked down.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of Step 29 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question from the order of the ברייתא against רב יוסף stays unresolved.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: anyone who has relations with one of the עריות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה: 'And so too one who has relations with any of the עריות.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And so too, one who has relations with any one of the עריות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a quote, not a new ruling. The משנה extends a law it taught earlier to anyone who has relations with any of the forbidden relatives. The גמרא is about to explain this line.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too, the same applies

phrases.english: And so too, one who has relations with one
of all the forbidden relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הַבָּא עַל אַחַת מִכׇּל הָעֲרָיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the חרש discussion to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה extends its rule to anyone who has relations with any of the עריות.

steps.title: רב עמרם introduces a teaching from רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם says that רב ששת told them something about this line, and the teaching itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: This matter רב ששת said to us,
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב עמרם announces that he heard a teaching from רב ששת on this topic, and the actual teaching comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No ruling has been given yet. The line only tells us who taught it, so we know the next words are רב ששת's teaching as reported by רב עמרם.

phrases.english: Rav Amram said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִלְּתָא אֲמַר לַן רַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: This matter Rav Sheshet said to us,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם: הָא מִלְּתָא אֲמַר לַן רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the explanation of the משנה line quoted in Step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line introduces רב ששת's teaching as reported by רב עמרם.
